result.markdown: # Functions ![](/images/function.png){style="width:200px; background: white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"} R __Functions__ allow the user to carry out specific tasks. R has many inbuilt __functions__ but you can also create your own. Currently we will look at inbuilt __functions__. ## Function layout The basic layout of a __function__ is (don't type the below into `R`): ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} function_name(objects, options) ``` ::: There are 3 main parts to the above: - The __function name__ (`function_name`) - The __object/s__ to provide to the __function__ - This can be numbers, strings, __variables__ we have created etc - Most __functions__ require at least one __object__ - Some __functions__ can take multiple objects, if multiple __objects__ are provided they must be separated by `,` - __Function__ options (`options`) - Options can be provided to some __functions__ to alter the way they will work - Some __functions__ don't have options - Most options have default modes. If the options is not specified the default mode will be used - Like __objects__, when using multiple options they must be separated by `,` ## Numerical rounding examples Try running the below commands in your Rstudio __console__ which utilise 4 different __functions__. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ceiling(3.5) floor(3.5) sqrt(9) round(3.5555, digits = 2) round(3.5555, digits = 3) round(3.5555, digits = 0) two <- sqrt(4) ``` ::: ## Help page You may be able to intuit what the above __functions__ do from their names and output. However, if you are not sure/would like to be certain you can look at the help pages of __functions__. The help page of __functions__ can be accessed in 2 main ways: - Click on the __function name__ so your cursor is in it and press __F1__. - Type `?` followed by the __function name__. Example below: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ?ceiling ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: :::
